instruction: Follow the API deployment logs in staging, starting with the last ten minutes and keeping only fifty initial lines.
context: kubectl logs: -n selects namespace, -f follows output, --since accepts a duration, and --tail limits the initial lines. These flags may be combined around the resource operand.

instruction: Run env inside the API pod in staging without allocating a terminal.
context: kubectl exec: -n selects namespace. A bare -- ends kubectl option parsing and separates the command executed in the container; -i and -t are only for interactive terminal sessions.

instruction: Show a compact decorated commit graph across every ref.
context: git log: --all walks all refs, --oneline selects compact output, --decorate adds ref names, and --graph draws ancestry. Each switch controls a distinct part of the view.

instruction: Summarize the files and line counts currently staged for commit.
context: git diff: --cached compares the index with HEAD; --stat prints a file-level summary instead of the patch. --cached is an alias for --staged.

instruction: Quietly follow redirects while downloading the release manifest, failing on HTTP errors and retrying three times.
context: curl: -f fails on HTTP errors, -s is silent, -S restores error messages, and -L follows redirects; compatible short switches may be bundled as -fsSL. --retry takes a count.

instruction: Fetch the health endpoint with a two-second connection limit and a ten-second total limit.
context: curl: --connect-timeout limits connection establishment; --max-time limits the complete transfer. Both options require duration values before the URL operand.

instruction: Mirror source into backup while preserving hard links, ACLs, extended attributes, and numeric ownership IDs.
context: rsync: -a is archive mode; -H preserves hard links, -A ACLs, and -X extended attributes. --numeric-ids avoids mapping user and group names. These additions are not implied by -a.

instruction: Preview an archive sync that would delete destination files absent from source, showing every proposed change.
context: rsync: -a enables archive behavior, -n is dry-run, --delete removes destination-only entries, and --itemize-changes describes planned updates. Dry-run should accompany deletion previews.

instruction: Run the unit tests quietly, stop at the first failure, and suppress the warnings summary.
context: pytest: -q reduces output, -x stops after the first failure, and --disable-warnings suppresses the warnings summary. The test path is an operand rather than an option value.

instruction: Run integration tests verbosely but stop after three failures and report the five slowest tests.
context: pytest: -v increases verbosity, --maxfail accepts a failure count, and --durations accepts how many slow tests to report. Equals-form keeps each option and value together.

instruction: Apply all Ruff fixes in src and tests, including fixes Ruff marks unsafe.
context: ruff check: --fix applies available edits and --unsafe-fixes opts into edits excluded from the safe set. Both source directories remain positional operands.

instruction: Check formatting for src and tests and print the proposed diff without changing files.
context: ruff format: --check returns failure when formatting differs and --diff prints proposed changes. Neither switch writes files when --check is active.

instruction: Noninteractively ask the deployment host for its uptime, giving connection setup five seconds.
context: ssh: -o introduces one configuration assignment. BatchMode=yes disables password prompts, while ConnectTimeout limits setup time. Each assignment needs its own -o.

instruction: Open a compressed SSH session that sends a keepalive every thirty seconds and disconnects after three missed replies.
context: ssh: -C enables compression. ServerAliveInterval sets seconds between protocol keepalives and ServerAliveCountMax controls tolerated missed replies; both use separate -o assignments.

instruction: Inspect the brief TLS handshake for example.com on port 443 while sending the correct SNI name.
context: openssl s_client: -connect takes HOST:PORT, -servername sets TLS SNI, and -brief reduces connection output. The hostname value is required separately by both options.

instruction: Test only TLS 1.3 against example.com and close stdin immediately after the handshake request.
context: openssl s_client: -tls1_3 restricts protocol negotiation; -connect and -servername retain separate values. Redirecting stdin from /dev/null prevents an interactive wait.

instruction: Search hidden files under the current directory for TODO with line numbers, excluding everything below .git.
context: rg: -n prints line numbers, --hidden includes hidden paths, and --glob applies a pattern. A leading ! in the glob excludes matching paths and must remain one argument.

instruction: Search Python files for the literal text user.id without treating the dot as a regex, ignoring case.
context: rg: -F selects fixed-string matching, -i ignores case, and --glob restricts paths. Option case matters: -F is not -f, which reads patterns from a file.

instruction: Emit null-delimited paths for regular files larger than one hundred megabytes below the current directory.
context: find: -type f selects regular files, -size +100M selects sizes strictly above 100 mebibytes on GNU find, and -print0 emits null-delimited pathnames.

instruction: List directories exactly two levels below src without descending beyond that level.
context: GNU find: -mindepth excludes shallower entries and -maxdepth prevents deeper descent. Equal values select exactly one depth; -type d restricts results to directories.

instruction: Show nginx warnings and more severe messages since today without invoking a pager.
context: journalctl: -u filters one unit, --since takes a time expression, -p filters by priority range, and --no-pager writes directly to the terminal.

instruction: Print kernel messages from the previous boot in reverse chronological order without a pager.
context: journalctl: -k restricts to kernel messages, -b accepts a boot offset such as -1, -r reverses order, and --no-pager disables paging. The -1 token is the value of -b.

instruction: List failed service units, including inactive units, without opening a pager.
context: systemctl list-units: --type filters unit type, --state filters active state, --all includes inactive units, and --no-pager disables paging.

instruction: Show only the active and sub states of the current user's sync service.
context: systemctl: --user addresses the user manager. show emits properties, and each selected property uses a separate --property option; repeating it preserves multiple fields.

instruction: Display src as a two-level tree with hidden entries, long metadata, and Git status.
context: eza: --tree enables tree view, --level limits its depth, --all includes hidden entries, --long adds metadata, and --git adds repository status. --level requires a value.

instruction: List all entries in long form, putting directories first and sorting newest modification time first.
context: eza: --group-directories-first groups directories, --sort=modified selects modification time, and --reverse makes newest entries appear first for that ordering. --all and --long affect visibility and detail.

instruction: Benchmark make test after three warmup runs, performing at least ten measured runs and exporting JSON results.
context: hyperfine: --warmup takes a count, --min-runs sets the minimum measured runs, and --export-json takes an output path. The benchmark command must remain a single shell argument.

instruction: Compare compression levels one through nine with two warmups, substituting each level into gzip.
context: hyperfine: --parameter-scan takes a parameter name, minimum, and maximum. The command template follows as one argument and references the parameter in braces; --warmup takes a count.
